div.head: List of Papers
div.p: [Incoming papers are listed chronologically under date of receipt. Unless otherwise specified, the correspondence is from or to officials in the Department of State.]
PART I: THE CONTINUATION OF THE WAR—PARTICIPATION OF THE UNITED STATES

p.hi: The Conduct of the War—Discussions Regarding Peace
preparations for the entrance of the united states into the war

row.cell: From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
Proposes to compile résumé of British wartime legislation, etc., found to be of practical working value.

Authorization to compile résumé of British wartime legislation, etc.

Inquiry regarding previous report on British handling of censorship, registration of aliens, etc., on outbreak of the war.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.): from Bell
Locates desired reports concerning British handling of censorship, registration of aliens, etc., on outbreak of the war.
To the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
Request for data concerning precautionary measures taken by belligerents during the war.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
Recommendation that U. S. admiral be sent to London for formal establishment of interchange of naval information and cooperation.
To the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
Suggests interview with British Foreign Trade Bureau regarding cooperation.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
British suggestion that upon entering the war the United States furnish troops immediately and establish liaison office in France.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
States that much time was lost by Great Britain during early part of the war because of delayed action along certain lines.
To the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
Notification that an admiral will be sent to Great Britain to establish closer naval relations.
To the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
Cooperation in handling shipping, munitions, and finances discussed with member of British Embassy.
French mission to the United States proposed.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
British mission to the United States, headed by Balfour, proposed.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.): Lassiter to Kuhn
British offer of assistance in the United States in organizing censorship and training the army.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
Recommends establishment of mission of experts by each of the two Governments in the Capital of the other.

p.hi: the announcement of a state of war between the united states and germany, april 6—plans of cooperation with the allied powers: the british and french special missions

row.cell: To diplomatic representatives in all countries except Russia (tel.)
Announcement of a state of war between the United States and Germany.
Morgenthau suggests representing to Turkey the advantages in maintaining friendly relations with the United States.

A French mission will be welcomed.
To the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
A British mission will be welcomed.
Suggests that French and British Governments consult together in arranging visits of their respective missions to the United States.

p.hi: severance of relations by austria-hungary, april 8—efforts to maintain relations with turkey—efforts to counteract agitation for peace in russia—plans of naval, military, and economic assistance to the allied powers

row.cell: Quotes Austro-Hungarian note of Apr. 8, announcing severance of diplomatic relations with the United States.
Turkey’s confidence of early peace encouraged by Germany. Rumors of Russian separate peace increase hope.
Suggests plan to induce Turkey to abandon Germany and negotiate with the Entente.
Efforts to maintain friendly relations with Turkey.
Russia informed of U. S. entry into the war against Germany. Investigation regarding negotiations for separate peace.
Peace terms which German Socialists would have their Government accept.
Instructions to investigate report of possible peace terms between Germany and Russia.
To the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
British commissioners are invited to become guests of the United States.
French commissioners are invited to become guests of the United States.
Personnel and approximate date of visit of French mission to the United States.
Information that Great Britain and France have sent committees to Petrograd in effort to counteract agitation for separate peace.
Swedish press reports that Russian labor and military representatives deliberate on Russian foreign policy and continuation of the war.
Interview with Miliukov on Socialists’ attitude toward separate peace. Revival of war spirit by Government.

Reports submarine situation, recommending prompt U. S. cooperation.
Message from representatives of American Jewry to Foreign Minister offering cooperation with Russian brethren in opposing separate peace.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
British request that unit of troops be sent to England and France, and regiment of Irishmen from the United States be trained in Ireland.
Tangible evidence that the United States is in the war might help nullify separate peace proposals in Russia.
Chief of Military Mission with the French Army to The Adjutant General (tel.)
Quotes French recommendations regarding U. S. military cooperation.
Political situation in Greece; advisability of sending diplomatic representative to Salonica.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.): to the President
The Prime Ministers of Great Britain and France to go to Italy for conference about possible peace with Austria.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.): from Sims
Report on submarine operations and recommendations for opposing them.
Berlin press reports demonstrations against cutting of bread rations and a strong; desire for peace.
To the Ambassador in Russia (tel.): McRoberts to H. F. Meserve
Statement that separate peace may prevent Russian participation in U. S. loan.
Requests report on general conditions in Russia for publication, if facts warrant, to allay fears of separate peace.

Conference in France regarding Russian situation and Italian interests in eastern Mediterranean.
Suggests that the united States organize military hospitals for service in England and abroad, for use temporarily by the British.
Presents note of Russian Government on needs for the naval defense of Russian Arctic coast.
Report on Allied conference in France.
Italian mission to the United States announced. Socialist demonstration against war threatened.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.): from Sims
Reports situation and urges maximum naval assistance immediately.

p.hi: severance of relations by turkey, april 20—denials of russia’s intention to make a separate peace—the french plan of military cooperation—the situation with respect to submarine warfare: naval cooperation—the italian special mission—the situation in greece

row.cell: From the Secretary of Embassy in Turkey (tel.)
Turkey severs diplomatic relations with the United States.
Russian assurances of no separate peace.
For publication: statement of Russian attitude toward separate peace.
Information given by an American from Berlin regarding conditions in Germany and attitude toward the United States.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.): Sims to the President and the Secretary of the Navy
Further report on submarine operations and recommendations for opposing them.
In Russian-American meeting Russian officials show enthusiasm for U. S. recognition and deny intention of separate peace.

Statement made by German Radical Socialist regarding basis for peace negotiations.
Report on conference between Joffre and Chief of Staff, U. S. A.

Presents program of military cooperation which France desires the United States to undertake.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.): Sims to the Secretary of the
Report on critical situation caused by increased number of submarines operating.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
Reports critical situation caused by submarine successes and recommends immediate dispatch of all U.S. anti-submarine craft.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.): Sims to Secretary of Navy
Reports pressing need of vessels, with repair and supply facilities to help break enemy submarine morale.
Personnel of Italian mission to the United States.
Department’s questions relative to parliamentary elections and dissolution of Parliament not answered.
Greece seeks U.S. assistance to secure raising of Entente blockade.
Request for participation in conferences between U. S. naval authorities and British commissioners regarding naval cooperation.
Greek Provisional Government has sent commissioners to the United States to enlist volunteers to fight against Bulgaria and Germany.
Object of British and French missions in the United States and of proposed Root mission to Russia.
Differences regarding Russia’s foreign policy adjusted satisfactorily without disturbances.
Proposed action by Venizelist commissioners in the United States impossible at present.
Delivery of vessels ordered by Russia is promised, but sending of U. S. patrol boats to White Sea impossible at present.

p.hi: note and declaration of the russian provisional government on the aims of the war, communicated may 3—message of the american federation of labor to the council of workmen’s and soldiers’ deputies on the terms of peace—discussions with the french and british missions—arrival of a permanent french high commissioner, tardieu—dispatch of the staff of the american expeditionary force—relations with bulgaria

row.cell: Presents Foreign Minister’s statement of Russia’s aims in the war. Enclosure: proclamation of the Provisional Government.
New ministry to be formed in Greece.
Notes on conference with British Special Mission

Reply to request for participation in conferences between U.S. naval authorities and British commissioners regarding naval cooperation.
Message from American Federation of Labor to Executive Committee of Council of Workmen’s and Soldiers’ Deputies in Russia urging united action against Prussian militarism.
From the Head of the British Special Mission
Proposes discussion of munitions and form of assistance the United States will render.
Official explanation of Ministry’s note of May 3, which appeases Workman’s Committee.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.): Sims to Secretary of Navy
Reports heavy loss to shipping; urgently recommends augmenting of naval forces.
Press report of discussion in German Diet of disposition of Belgium and deportation of Belgian workmen.
Press statement of report in Reichstag on unexpected success of submarine warfare and confidence in final result.
Germany aids Russian pacifists in returning to Russia to work for separate peace.
Inquiry regarding subjects to be taken up with proposed Japanese mission to the United States.
Recommends course to be pursued in sending Japanese mission to
Presents Foreign Minister’s note setting forth policy of Greece toward the war.

To the Minister in Denmark (tel.); the same to the Ministers in Switzerland and the Netherlands
Instructions to watch German press for comments on America’s delay in entering the war.
Secheidemann’s address before the Reichstag on peaceful settlement of European boundaries.
Serious situation in Greece: suggestion that the United States urge Allies to send relief and lift blockade.
To the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.); mutatis mutandis, to the Ambassador in France
Announcement of sailing date of commander of American expedition and staff. Instructions.
From the Consul General at Sofia (tel.)
Bulgaria gives assurances of continued friendly relations with the United States.
From the Head of the British Special Mission
Notes on important subjects concerning the war discussed during stay of British mission at Washington.

p.hi: the president’s message of may 22 to the russian provisional government on the objects of the united states in the war—initial measures of active american participation in the war—the belgian, rumanian, and japanese special missions—the mission of lord north-cliffe—statements of the french premier and senate on the terms of peace—developments in greece: the abdication of king constantine

row.cell: Quotes for publication the President’s message to the Russian Provisional Government on U.S. objects in entering the war.
From the Assistant Secretary of the Treasury
Questions certain wording in proposed cablegram to Petrograd concerning credit for Russia.
To the Assistant Secretary of the Treasury
Change of wording in telegram sent to Petrograd regarding Russian credit.
From the Head of the British Special Mission
Problem of reciprocal rates for Allied purchases in America and U. S. purchases in Europe.
Presents Japanese telegram proposing a special mission to the United States.
Re arrival in the United States of the French High Commissioner.
For publication: measures adopted by the United States for active participation in the war.
Arrival at Queenstown of flotilla of U. S. torpedo-boat destroyers; official welcome.
To the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
Quotes, for publication in Great Britain, text of communication from the President to the Russian Provisional Government.
Personnel and sailing date of Belgian mission to the United States.
Gratification at assurances of Russian Provisional Government to fulfill engagements made to the Allies.
Acknowledges receipt of Foreign Minister’s note on conditions influencing Greek attitude toward the war.
To diplomatic representatives in European countries (tel.)
Instructions to make public denial of statement published by Georg Bernhard and alleged to have been made by Gerard.
Austrian Emperor’s speech before Parliament on constitutional rights and willingness to make peace.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.): Sims to Navy Department
Report on activity of submarines and work of U. S. destroyers.
U. S. naval forces to concentrate in one area, thus releasing British forces to protect Russian Arctic route.

America’s greatest service would be to send to Europe skilled mechanics under military discipline.
From the Consul A at Liverpool
Arrival in Liverpool of Base Hospital No. 4, U. S. Army; British official welcome.
Informed that British forces will be withdrawn from Macedonia. Reasons.
Personnel and sailing date or Rumanian mission to the United States.

Requests report regarding proposed Northcliffe mission to the United States.

Northcliffe sent to the United States on commercial not diplomatic errand.
Quotes press statements on difficulties of securing tonnage for transporting and maintaining U. S. troops
From the Chargé in the Netherlands (tel.)
Quotes press statement on interviews between Gerard and Bernhard in which former charges are repeated.
England, France, and Russia agree on policy regarding Greek affairs and send special emissary to Greece.
French Premier’s speech and Senate resolution on terms of peace.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
Arrival of General Pershing and staff in London.
Bernhard’s utterances are branded as German method of endeavoring to create distrust among the Allies.
Instructions to report on Greek affairs, especially details of Allied agreement.
Informed that Entente plans removal of Greek King, substituting a regent with French High Commissioner in control.
Reported that Turkey is desirous of separate peace but is urged by Germany to await results of submarine campaign.
Reports development of political affairs in Greece; King preparing to abdicate.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.):
Quotes General Smuts’s message stating America can win the war with airplanes.
Captain Persius discusses in German press importance of America’s participation in the war.
Personnel and sailing date of Japanese special mission to the United States.
Circumstances attending the King’s departure; Alexander takes oath.
To the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.); the same to the Ambassadors in France and Italy
Negotiation with Allied air services for joint program of airplane construction.
Entente powers to recognize King Alexander. Significance of political developments.
Japanese special mission will be welcomed. Names and titles of personnel requested.

p.hi: the president’s flag day address, june 14—the submarine situation: american naval policy—the status of greece—refusal of the united states to participate in the inter-allied conference on balkan affairs—the morgenthau-frankfurter mission to europe—the struggle over electoral reform and peace terms in germany

row.cell: To the diplomatic representatives in certain countries (tel.)
For publication: text of the President’s Flag Day address.
To the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
Saw-mill units donated to Great Britain by New England States.
Interview with the King on war problems.
Recommends that a division of U. S. destroyers be sent to Russia.
Quotes Entente ultimatum demanding abdication of King Constantine, and correspondence between High Commissioner and President of Council.
Date set for departure to the United States of Japanese special mission; names and titles of personnel.
Germany challenges President Wilson’s change of policy and aims in entering the war, as expressed in his note to Russia.
Continuation of Germany’s remarks on President Wilson’s note to Russia.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.); to the President also
Seriousness of submarine gains and necessity for prompt action by anti-submarine craft.
Notification of raising of blockade of Greece.
To the Consul at Alexandria (tel.): to Philip
Instructions to assist Morgenthau in efforts to ameliorate Jewish conditions in Palestine.

Question of Allied assistance to Norway in case it is driven into the war.
Negotiations between Venizelos cabinet and Zaimis Government for union of Greece.

Instructions to arrange for Morgenthau to meet British representative at Gibraltar.
Instructions to arrange for Morgenthau to meet French and British representatives at Gibraltar.

Purpose of Japanese special mission to the United States.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)

Greece’s new Ministry; statement of foreign policy.
Status of relations between Greece and the Central powers.

Critical situation caused by submarine activity. Need of armed small craft for protection of British and French coasts.

Announcement of U. S. naval policy and general plan of action in relation to the Allies.
Greece is at war with Germany and Bulgaria; relations are broken with other Central powers.

Criticism of British Admiralty methods; convoy system on adequate scale suggested; report and independent opinion requested.

From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.); to the President also
German Chancellor reported as willing to conclude peace without annexations or compensations.
From the Special Agents, Morgenthau and Frankfurter (tel.)
Report on situation in eastern theater of the war and opinion that time is not ripe for peace negotiations with Turkey.
Regrets inability to send destroyers to Russia as suggested.
Official suggestion that the United States send military aid to Italian front, supplying heavy artillery, etc.
To the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
The United States is not now ready to take part in inter-Allied war conferences.
From the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.): Sims to the President
Reports in detail shipping situation and gives independent opinion on steps to be taken.
Press reports of the Kaiser’s edict regarding reform in Prussian election laws.

Influences surrounding Greek King; his acceptance of ultimatum; details accompanying abdication.

Continuation of summary of Chancellor’s speech: statement of policy and internal conditions.
To the Ambassador in Great Britain (tel.)
The President is unwilling to have the United States represented at the Allied conference at Paris.
Status of Rumanian mission to the United States.
Instructions to remain in France until Frankfurter reports, and to refrain from discussion of U. S. policies.

p.hi: peace resolution of the german reichstag, july 19—the inter-allied conference on balkan affairs—partial revelation of secret agreements concerning asia minor—the american proposal of an inter-allied naval conference—the president’s reply to the request of the French government for his views on the organization of a society of nations—various discussions of peace terms

U. S. proposal of an inter-Allied naval conference.
Inquires nature of agreements between Allies concerning Asia Minor.

Text of the Pope’s appeal for peace.
Sweden invites conference of neutrals, including Switzerland, to discuss conditions of a durable peace.
To the diplomatic officers in Allied countries; also in Siam, Rumania, Corfu

Quotes Balfour’s message to British Minister to the Holy See regarding the Pope’s peace note.

States Greek objections to the Pope’s peace terms.

Press reports that Germany commends the Pope’s peace proposal.

German Chancellor discusses secret treaties of Allies and refusal of latter to consider peace.

Data suggested for meeting of inter Allied naval conference.

German press comments on break between Reichstag Majority and the Chancellor regarding peace resolution of July 19.
Belgium’s acknowledgment of the Pope’s peace note.

French views on the Pope’s appeal and on conflict between German Chancellor and Reichstag.
Quotes identic telegram from Associated Ministers at Jassy to their Governments conveying Prime Minister’s appeal for aid.

Text of the President’s reply of Aug. 27 to the Pope’s appeal for peace, sent via Great Britain.

France’s war policy as expressed by the Premier of the new Ministry.
